topic: Implementing opt-out functionality and database review
summary_markdown:
The discussion covered two main areas: implementing an opt-out mechanism, and reviewing ClickHouse database performance.

**Opt-Out Implementation:**
The goal is to create a dedicated opt-out page accessible via redirects. The proposed solution involves setting up a new public subdomain, `https://optout.allunite.com`, which will host the content. All existing URLs of the format `https://allunite.com/r/<alias>` must redirect to this new domain (`https://optout.allunite.com/r/<alias>`). The page design should maintain AllUnite branding and remove links to other sections.

**Database Review:**
A review of multiple ClickHouse instances showed that the performance metrics (e.g., node stats) were being monitored. It was noted that while high theoretical I/O bandwidth is possible, actual observed I/O on the company's ClickHouse clusters remained significantly lower (around 130 MB/sec), especially when simultaneous read and write operations occur.

The team also discussed advanced features like Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT) for hardware-accelerated compression in ClickHouse.
decisions: The opt-out page will be hosted on the subdomain https://optout.allunite.com
All existing redirects from https://allunite.com/r/<alias> must point to https://optout.allunite.com/r/<alias>
action_items: Investigate how to implement the opt-out page on WordPress (p1)
Test ClickHouse performance changes on a sandbox environment
